**Rationale (measured relations).** The calibration rows are a null result that constrains any mechanism: fitted slopes reproduce the nominal samples closely — S046 ≈0.459, S019 ≈0.189, S007 ≈0.070 N/cm from successive loading points — and loading/unloading gaps are tiny (S046 maximum gap ≈0.03 N; S007 ≈0.003 N). So the installed spring law is effectively linear and hysteresis-free within these tables, and the strong threshold structure must originate in geometry (moment arms ℓ, stop angles, mounting offsets), not spring constitutive nonlinearity. In pair_A, held at fixed geometry, the neighbour state translates the window but preserves its width (rotor 1 at ℓ=0: ±7.2 cm for both other-states; at ℓ=4.731: ±4.6 cm both), while increasing ℓ shrinks half-width monotonically 7.2→6.8→6.0→4.6 cm and grows the neighbour-induced centre shift from ≈0 to 1.2 cm (rotor 1) and ≈0 to 4.4 cm (rotor 2). The shift looks roughly linear in ℓ² (0.1, 0.6, 1.2 cm at ℓ=1.58, 3.15, 4.73). Pair_B, with ℓ fixed at 4.7, shows much larger neighbour bias — 11.1 cm (rotor 1: centres 2.6 vs 13.7) and 5.5 cm (rotor 2) — with widths nearly unchanged (4.1 vs 4.0; 11.4 vs 11.7).
